title: Elephant-cage HF antennas may have aided Sherman's downloads
place_text: San Vito dei Normanni Air Station, Italy; Offutt AFB, Nebraska

tellings.quote: antennas. Were these antennas and the signals they received somehow very important for the signals that Dan himself was trying [music] to decode for the NSA?

plain: Michels wonders whether the huge ring-shaped radio antennas known as "elephant cages", which pick up high-frequency signals at bases such as San Vito dei Normanni Air Station in Italy and Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska, were tied to the signals a former sergeant named Dan Sherman says he was decoding for the National Security Agency, the US signals intelligence agency, in the early 1990s. Sherman describes that work in his book Above Black, which Michels draws on. Michels puts it as an open question of his own, not as something Sherman claims.
